chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The divorce of the young boy (child) is not effective (null), so it does not contradict the two previous narrations, because the meaning in this narration is that we interpret it as referring to one who does not possess intellect and does not know how to divorce properly, because that (intellect/maturity) is considered for the validity of his divorce, which indicates that.
ai.seo_question: Is the divorce of a young child considered valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that a young boy's divorce is not effective because it is conditional upon possessing intellect ('aql) and the capacity to understand the act. This ruling aligns with the broader Shia jurisprudential principle that legal acts require both maturity and cognitive comprehension, distinguishing the 'sabi' (child) from the 'shabib' (young adult) who may have partial intellect.
